Definition: from Ὑμήν (the god of weddings); "hymenæal"; Hymenæus, an opponent of Christianity:--Hymenæus.
BiblicalUsage: Hymenaeus is a man Paul names twice, and both times as a warning. In 1 Timothy 1:20 Paul says he delivered Hymenaeus and Alexander unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme, and in 2 Timothy 2:17 he says their word eats as a canker. The life behind the name is told on the Hymenaeus People profile.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Hymenaeus matters because God names the men who shipwrecked their faith as surely as He names the faithful, and Hymenaeus is one of them.
